messages:
marco: FYI monitoring -> rack-12 (eu-west1) is showing repeated power-limit oscillations on a subset of nodes, plus fan tach dropouts on GPU 0 and GPU 3. Seeing Xid 13 and rising ECC correctable counters. Impact: elevated 95/99 tail latency on several inference routes.

marco: snippet from node gpu-12-03:
```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00.0): 13, PID 4621
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,temperature.gpu,utilization.gpu,power.draw --format=csv
0, 86 C, 98 %, 295 W
3, 78 C, 92 %, 305 W
ipmitool sdr list | grep -i fan
FAN1 | 1500 RPM | ok
FAN2 | 0 RPM | ns
```

eng-bot: Alert created: ALERT-2026-1812345678 -> GPU_THERMAL_RISE rack-12. Estimated affected nodes: 3. Notified eng-infra oncall.

sana: can we cordon/drain the affected nodes and shift inference to the backup pool? don't want noisy retries to hit customers.

oncall: I'm starting cordon on gpu-12-03 and gpu-12-07 now. Will move pods with graceful drain (30s). Confirming capacity in eu-west1-backup.

eli: before full replacement, try setting power limit -20W on the cards to reduce thermal spikes and see if fan tach stabilizes. Risk: slight perf drop but better than evictions. Command: `nvidia-smi -i 0 -pl 275` (current 295W).

lisa: backup pool has ~20% free, should absorb short reroute. But traffic for some SLAs can't tolerate the 95th increase; can we route those to dedicated-inference-east as temporary? That adds cross-region latency but keeps tail down.

marco: good plan. oncall, after cordon/drain, run `nvidia-healthmon` and `tegrastat` health checks and capture ECC counters. Paste outputs here.

oncall: cordon + drain done for gpu-12-03 and gpu-12-07. Moving 42 pods. Running quick checks.

oncall: health check output:
```
GPU 0 ECC: correctable +42 since boot
GPU 3 ECC: correctable +38 since boot
powercap oscillation events: 6 in last 10m
fan tach dropouts: observed 2x on GPU3
```

sana: sounds flaky hardware. recommend flagging for RMA but keep node in maintenance until we confirm replacement schedule.

eli: agree. For now I'll push a temporary routing policy: prefer eu-west1-backup for model:realtime-critical with fallback to dedicated-east. That should shave tail spikes while we RMA.

marco: also add automatic fallback to a lower-batch-size replica when powercap events detected (reduce batch from 8->4). We'll test rollout in canary for 10% traffic first.

lisa: cost note — routing to dedicated-east will increase egress and instance cost. I'll post an ask to finance for a temporary buffer if this persists.

eng-bot: Incident state: mitigation in progress. Runbook reference: infra/runbooks/gpu-thermal-powercap.md

oncall: scheduling vendor RMA for 2026-03-21 09:00 UTC for the two flaky cards. Meanwhile nodes remain in maintenance. Confirmed no further evictions after drain, tail latency dropped ~30% on affected routes.

marco: thanks team. keep monitoring; if oscillations reappear after power-limit tweak we'll escalate to full rack power supply replacement. I'll follow up with a short postmortem once RMA completes.
